clue.text: Most painful, therefore take a break

parts.note: so means therefore, as in 'it rained, so we stayed in'
to rest is to take a break from work

explanation.surface: Someone in great pain concludes they had better stop and rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of sore, which describes something hurting or tender.

clue.text: Prison warder's pay?

explanation.surface: A question about what a prison officer earns.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: a prison officer is a 'screw', and 'screw' is also old slang for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison slang calls a jailer this, and old slang uses the same word for wages or salary.

clue.text: Races a lot — wildly moving steps

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of races a lot are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone racing about a great deal on a staircase that moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges RACESALOT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical staircase is a set of steps that moves passengers up or down.

clue.text: So pilot fell to earth

indicators.note: fell suggests a crash, so the letters of so pilot tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot crashes his aircraft to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' rearranges SOPILOT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper layer of soil is the earth in which plants grow.

clue.text: VAT files put in order for holiday

indicators.note: put in order tells us to arrange the letters of vat files differently

explanation.surface: Tidying the tax paperwork before going away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in order' rearranges VATFILES. VAT is the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive day or season of celebration is a holiday.

clue.text: Make eager haste, but be tripped by own naughty child

parts.note: to be tripped by something is to fall over it
one's means own, as in one's own home
an elf is a mischievous little creature, a word also used of a naughty child

explanation.surface: A parent rushing about trips over their own unruly youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as FALL OVER ONE'S ELF; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being overly keen, rushing to do something with great eagerness.

clue.text: More secure job as ostler?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a stable-hand's work offers better security.
explanation.walkthrough: An ostler looks after horses at an inn, so he is one who stables them: a 'stabler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of steady meaning firmer; also, whimsically, a person who houses horses in a stable.

clue.text: Having differences, competing about a run

indicators.note: about here means around, so the word for competing wraps the other letters

parts.note: vying means competing
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Rival athletes disagreeing while competing over a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that differ from one another are said to change or diverge, being unlike each other.

clue.text: Not a busy series of months, by a very long way

definitions.text: Not a busy series of months

explanation.surface: A quiet year is contrasted with an enormous distance.
explanation.walkthrough: First read the answer as an untaxing twelve months; second as an astronomical distance. 'by' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical unit measuring the distance light travels in a year; also, jokingly, a year with little work.

clue.text: Military policeman's bird

explanation.surface: A soldier in the military police and his pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: British military police wear red caps, hence the nickname; it is also an old name for the goldfinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname for a British army police officer, and a dialect name for the goldfinch, a songbird.

clue.text: After spring, little creature is game

indicators.note: after says the creature follows the word for spring

parts.note: a spring is a jump or leap
a frog is a small amphibian

explanation.surface: Once spring arrives, a small animal is fair prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's pastime of vaulting over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Prosperous, but we will fuss

parts.note: we'll is the contraction of we will
a to-do is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A wealthy person anticipating that they will make a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy, comfortably off financially.

clue.text: A trial results in rope

indicators.note: results in says the letters of a trial produce something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A court case ending with a hanging rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'results in' rearranges ATRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso, a long noosed cord used by cowboys.

clue.text: Harmless story of blameless situation

parts.note: white can mean innocent or blameless, as in whiter than white
the lie of something, as in the lie of the land, is its position or situation

explanation.surface: A harmless tale told about an innocent state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small untruth told to spare feelings, a fib meant kindly.

clue.text: Blown about by turns, was crying

parts.note: winds means turns, as a road winds
wept means was crying

explanation.surface: Someone tossed by twists and turns was in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed to strong gales, so battered or ruffled by the air.

clue.text: Caribbean music played for example in odd gear

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation sits inside the scrambled letters
odd means peculiar, telling us gear has its letters scrambled

explanation.surface: Jamaican music performed by people in strange clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns GEAR into RGAE, and 'in' puts EG inside: R-EG-GAE. 'played' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of popular music from Jamaica with a strong offbeat rhythm.

clue.text: Thorough searches for beauty

parts.note: good can mean thorough, as in a good clean
looks are searches, as in having a look for something

explanation.surface: Thorough hunts to find something beautiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive appearance, being handsome or pretty.

clue.text: New weapon's restricted

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A newly designed weapon is subject to controls.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited in width or scope, confined.

clue.text: Hooligan demolishes funfair

indicators.note: demolishes says the letters of funfair are knocked apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A thug wrecks the fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolishes' rearranges FUNFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent lawless person, a thug.

clue.text: Power needed to carry on round a race

indicators.note: round says the word for carry on surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to wage war is to carry it on
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Energy required to keep going round a racing circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: W-ATT-AGE. 'needed to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical power measured in watts.

clue.text: Look-see as complete

parts.note: once can mean as soon as, as in once you arrive
over means finished or complete

explanation.surface: Treating a quick glance as a finished job.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick inspection or cursory examination.

clue.text: Primitive type held me up in Irish county

indicators.note: held says the county name contains the other letters

parts.note: Cavan is a county in Ireland

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word me is read backwards

explanation.surface: An ancient person detained the speaker in rural Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ME into EM, which 'held' puts inside CAVAN: CAV-EM-AN. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric human, a primitive person living in caves.

clue.text: Piece under arch is off its position, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says only part of the following words is used, the answer lying within them

explanation.surface: An architectural part has shifted out of place slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'iS OFF ITs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Architectural term for the underside of an arch, beam or eave.

clue.text: It provides cover for a correspondent

definitions.text: It provides cover for a correspondent

parts.words: It provides cover for a correspondent
parts.note: a correspondent sounds like a writer, but read it as a letter, the thing posted, which this paper wrapper covers

explanation.surface: Something that protects a journalist working abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper wrapper in which a posted letter is sealed.

clue.text: Points to girl to follow

parts.note: E and N are compass points: east and north
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone gesturing towards a young woman to go after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and the second 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a result, to happen next.

clue.text: Leave the country, arriving at last in Middle Eastern state

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the state

parts.note: an emirate is a state ruled by an emir, as in the Gulf

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word arriving

explanation.surface: Someone departs home and finally settles in a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives G from 'arriving', and 'in' places it in EMIRATE: EMI-G-RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To move permanently abroad, departing one's homeland.

clue.text: New Zealanders almost rise, following revolutionary leader

indicators.note: following says the shortened word comes after the leader

parts.note: Mao Zedong led the Chinese communist revolution

indicators.note: almost says the word rise is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: People in New Zealand nearly revolt behind a radical chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E of 'rise' to give RIS, placed after MAO.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: No use thus as a player — unable to recognise the pitch

definitions.text: No use thus as a player

explanation.surface: A musician hopeless at hearing notes, or a cricketer who cannot read the wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pitch' suggests a sports field, but it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to distinguish musical notes, so useless as a performer of music.

clue.text: Get oneself comfortable in the finest leisure wear

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Relaxing in luxurious loungewear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'fiNEST LEisure'; 'the' and 'wear' are padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle snugly and cosily into a comfortable position.
